neighbours.label: the noun that completes a canonical numbered set (seven dwarfs, twelve apostles, eight trigrams, seven angels); the same number before an ordinary noun, or the set noun without its number, stays weaker
fire: The children dressed up as the three musketeers for the school play.
Moses came down the mountain carrying the ten commandments.
The chapel windows show the twelve disciples at the last supper.
A fortune teller laid out the sixty-four hexagrams of the I Ching.
The poet invoked the nine muses at the start of the epic.
Pilgrims believe the seven archangels guard the gates of heaven.
The story of the three wise men is told every December.
Medieval sermons warned against the seven deadly sins.
quiet: The children dressed up as pirates and soldiers for the school play.
Moses came down the mountain carrying two heavy stones.
The chapel windows show a crowd of fishermen at the shore.
A fortune teller laid out sixty-four cards on the table.
The poet thanked his nine cousins at the start of the speech.
Pilgrims believe the archangels guard the gates of heaven.
The story of three lost hikers was told on the news.
There were seven bicycles locked to the fence outside.

notes: Probes: eight trigrams 1.25, seven angels 0.76, seven dwarfs 0.69, twelve apostles 0.51; seven cars 0.02, angels without a number 0.17. Ordinals (sixth chapter 0.37, sixth element 0.25) fire too, so the near misses avoid them.
